title: Check if the Sentence Is Pangram
description:
# Check if the Sentence Is Pangram

A **pangram** is a sentence that contains every letter of the English alphabet at least once.

Given a string `sentence` containing only lowercase English letters, return `true` if `sentence` is a pangram. Otherwise, return `false`.

## Example 1:

**Input:** sentence = "thequickbrownfoxjumpsoverthelazydog"

**Output:** true

**Explanation:** Every lowercase English letter from `a` through `z` appears at least once.

## Example 2:

**Input:** sentence = "leetcode"

**Output:** false

**Explanation:** Several letters, including `a`, `b`, and `f`, never appear.

## Constraints:

* `1 <= sentence.length <= 1000`
* `sentence` consists only of lowercase English letters.

solutions.name: Boolean Seen Array With Count
solutions.description:
## Approach

Keep a boolean array of 26 slots, one for each lowercase English letter. When a letter is seen for the first time, mark its slot and increase a unique-letter counter.

## Key Insight

A pangram is exactly the moment when the unique-letter counter reaches 26, so the scan can return early once every slot has been discovered.

## Complexity Analysis

- Time Complexity: O(n)
- Space Complexity: O(1)

solutions.name: HashSet Unique Letters
solutions.description:
## Approach

Insert each character into a `HashSet`. The set automatically removes duplicates, so its size is the number of different letters that have appeared so far.

## Key Insight

Although a set is a general-purpose structure, the alphabet bounds it to at most 26 entries; reaching size 26 proves the sentence is a pangram.

## Complexity Analysis

- Time Complexity: O(n)
- Space Complexity: O(1)

solutions.name: Twenty Six Bit Mask
solutions.description:
## Approach

Use the low 26 bits of an integer as a compact seen table. For each character, set the bit at position `c - 'a'` and compare the mask with the mask where all 26 bits are set.

## Key Insight

Each lowercase letter maps to exactly one bit, so the full pangram state can be represented by `(1 << 26) - 1`.

## Complexity Analysis

- Time Complexity: O(n)
- Space Complexity: O(1)

solutions.name: Alphabet Index Scan
solutions.description:
## Approach

Instead of scanning the sentence and recording letters, scan the alphabet from `a` to `z`. For each required letter, ask whether that letter appears anywhere in the sentence.

## Key Insight

This reverses the viewpoint: a sentence is a pangram only if no required alphabet letter has `indexOf` equal to `-1`.

## Complexity Analysis

- Time Complexity: O(26n)
- Space Complexity: O(1)
